subject: Emotions
title: The Hedonic Treadmill
description: A fast breakdown of The Hedonic Treadmill for builders.

hook.text: Lottery winners return to their baseline happiness within a year. So do people who become paralyzed.

buildup.text: Philip Brickman's 1978 study shocked psychology. Major life changes barely moved the happiness needle long-term.

discovery.text: The hedonic treadmill means we adapt to both good and bad. Joy from new things fades as the brain recalibrates.

twist.text: This explains why buying things doesn't last. The new car thrills for weeks, then becomes 'just the car.'

climax.text: The treadmill has a purpose: it keeps you striving. If joy lasted forever, you'd stop pursuing anything new.

quiz.question: What is the hedonic treadmill?
options: People adapt back to baseline happiness after changes
